title: Great Mosque of Samarra and its spiral minaret
summary: The Great Mosque of Samarra, in the Abbasid capital in Iraq, was built between 849 and 852 and at 264 m by 159 m was the largest mosque in the Islamic world at the time. Its spiral minaret, al-Malwiya, has a square base 32 m on a side and rises 54 m.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS gives the construction years 849 to 852; UNESCO says only the 9th century. End is the present: the ruined mosque and minaret survive.

reviewer_note: Shape tower for the Malwiya spiral minaret (the sources opened do not describe its profile beyond 'five circular layers rise forming a huge spiral tower'). ICOMOS: square base sides 32 m, tower 54 m high; a travel caption seen in search results gave 52 m and 33 m and was not opened. The 849-852 dates cover the mosque; ICOMOS does not date the minaret separately. UNESCO's property point (34.08, 43.92) is an area centre kilometres away; OSM objects were used, so the OSM objects and Wikidata were the coordinate sources.
